catalog_quote: Stress is not a prominent feature of Palu’e, but it can be contrastive, which it is not in Indonesian. The disyllabic structure tends to level out stress. When there is stress, it falls on the penultimate syllable, unless it contains a schwa /ə/, as in the following example: nera [nəˈra] ‘think’; néra [ˈneːra] ‘lontar leaf mug’. Stress is not marked in the wordlist for these reasons. ... [fn. 88, item 216 tebha [təˀɓa]:] The stress is on the ultimate syllable, preceded by glottalization, as is the rule for [ɓ] preceded by schwa. ... [fn. 59, item 109 dhana [dana]:] The stress is on the first syllable ...

audit.recode_to: Drop the hedge (weight-hedged/weight-sensitive (tentative) -> unhedged): regular right-edge trochaic stress on the penult; a schwa penult cannot bear stress, stress then final (Danerek nera [nəˈra], Fernandez [kəˈja], Donohue kəˈru); add the secondary-stress rule/domain facts from Donohue: genitive and aspect enclitics (-gu/-ku, -mo, -n(e), -de/-te, -ʔu) are outside the stress domain (host+enclitic = antepenultimate stress), proclitic ak- is inside; monosyllabic roots surface long and stressed; compounds carry one foot per lexical morpheme (secondary stress). Kind: either keep what counts as heavy: full-vs-reduced-vowel without the hedge, or (following Donohue's explicit 'no weight' analysis with epenthetic schwa) code as fixed penultimate, quantity-insensitive, with epenthetic ə invisible to stress - the compilers should pick per catalog convention for epenthetic schwa. Cite Donohue MS as primary, Danerek 2019 and Fernandez 1989 as confirming.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim at the stated locators in the Danerek 2019 text we hold. (2) The record rests on a 2019 orthography/variation article whose author calls stress 'not prominent' and 'levelled'; two other descriptions - Donohue's dedicated stress MS (held held by the project since 9/13 but unused by this record) and Fernandez 1989 (downloaded now, scanned, p. 93) - both describe stress as regular penultimate with shift to the ultima when the penult is schwa, matching our the primary-stress rule exactly, so the surface coding (right edge, penult, schwa-avoidance) is safe. What the better source changes is (a) the hedge: Donohue treats stress as fully regular and foot-based, contradicting Danerek's 'weak/levelled' framing that drove the weight-sensitive (tentative) grade, and (b) missing domain facts (enclitics extrametrical -> antepenult; proclitic footed; monosyllable lengthening; per-morpheme feet), and (c) possibly the kind label, s
